text:
maria: quick heads-up — I ran a cross-cloud latency/99.9 sweep for the A100 80GB SKU using the same driver + CUDA (driver 525.60, CUDA 11.8). results look fine for throughput, but Azure shows a weird long tail on p99.9 for short-seq (64 tokens).
lee: can you paste the numbers?
maria: summary: AWS p50=8.2ms p95=12.1ms p99.9=28.3ms; GCP p50=8.4ms p95=12.5ms p99.9=27.9ms; Azure p50=8.5ms p95=13.0ms p99.9=72.8ms.
sam: wow, 72.8ms p99.9 is high. did you run same contention profile / node type?
maria: yes — same VM SKU family, isolated nodes, no other user load. configs identical: instance type, BIOS perf profile, kernel 5.10 on all.
jyoti: can you share the bench command and env? also any hotplug or live-migration events?
maria: bench command (short seq):
```
./redwood-bench --model /models/llama2-13b --seq 64 --batch 1 --driver 525.60 --cuda 11.8 --warmup 100 --iters 500 --measure p50,p95,p99,p999
```
(we used pinned cpus + isolated cgroups, --no-preempt enabled in kernel cmdline on test nodes)
lee: any kernel logs around the time of the tail events?
maria: attached a small snippet — i grabbed dmesg around a 72ms spike: "[timestamp] nvme0: timeout (cmd 0x1a)" then GPU driver recovered. not sure if nvme though, since model lives on ramdisk for bench.
sam: could be device interrupt storm or PCIe link retrain. Azure tends to be aggressive on power/thermal steering on some SKUs. did you monitor pstate/clocks?
maria: yes, we logged GPU clocks for the run. majority steady at 1.41GHz, but during spikes one GPU showed sudden drop to 300MHz for ~10ms then back.
jyoti: that sounds like clock-governor hiccup. what firmware/SMC versions on the Azure machines?
maria: Azure node reported microcode v1.2.3, AWS/GCP have v1.1.8. weird that newer microcode would cause throttle.
bench-bot: automated-bench: added run artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/1749201122/. includes raw traces, perf counters, and GPU clock logs.
lee: can we reproduce by doing power/thermal stress to trigger governor on AWS/GCP? if not reproducible it's likely platform-specific driver/firmware combo.
sam: also validate PCIe link speed (gen3 vs gen4) in all clouds, sometimes host BIOS forces gen3 causing occasional link retrain on heavy bursts.
maria: initial PCIe checks show gen4 on all hosts. I also saw a few AER (Advanced Error Reporting) messages on Azure: "AER: corrected error" timestamps near spike.
jyoti: AER corrected errors could indicate transient link issues causing GPU to stall briefly. ask infra to open a ticket with Azure with AER dumps + nvlink/pci logs. include the dmesg and perf samples.
maria: filing now. infra-bot: created ticket AZ-PCI-1749201122 in infra queue and attached the AER dump. ETA for cloud vendor triage ~48-72h. :thumbsup:
lee: meanwhile, two quick experiments to isolate: (1) repeat with different driver (e.g., 525.85) to see if driver change removes spikes; (2) run with small synthetic kernel that touches PCIe heavily to try to force AER.
maria: scheduling both. i'll run driver delta first. any ideas about quantization effects? we also ran q4 setups and saw slightly lower tails but not resolved.
sam: q4 reduces memory movement a bit, so minor improvement possible. but this sounds infra-level, not model-level.
jyoti: note for ticket: include kernel boot params, bios settings (pcie_aspm, pcie_link_speed), and any host-side NVMe events — vendor triage often asks for those.
maria: added BIOS dump + kernel cmdline + perf top samples to S3. link in ticket.
bench-bot: perf summary CSV uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/1749201122/summary.csv
lee: thanks — after infra/vendor triage, if they say platform ok we should try: - run swapping to older microcode - reproduce with a microbench that uses only kernel dispatch (no nvme) - probe if kernel 5.10 vs 5.15 changes behavior
maria: noted. i'll run the microcode rollback test and a kernel 5.15 image tomorrow. will report back.
sam: sounds good. if vendor blames link/firmware we'll add a transient fallback in runtime: detect GPU stall > 10ms and route that request to a compatible spare pool to avoid user-visible p99 issues. small mitigation until vendor fix.
jyoti: +1 on mitigation. create an RFC in eng-runtime to track fallback behavior.
maria: created draft RFC: /docs/rfc/fallback-on-gpu-stall.md and linked in ticket. will update thread once we have vendor response.
lee: cheers, thanks for the data — this is exactly the kind of cross-cloud skew we want to catch before customer impact. :rocket:
